chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Torah was revealed in the six days that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Gospel was revealed in the twelve that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Psalms were revealed in the eighteen that passed from the month of Ramadan, and the Criterion (Quran) was revealed 'on the Night of Power'.

key_terms.اَلتَّوْرَاةُ: The Torah, revealed to Prophet Musa (AS)
key_terms.اَلزَّبُورُ: The Psalms, revealed to Prophet Dawud (AS)
key_terms.اَلْفُرْقَانُ: The Criterion, referring to the Quran
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Decree, associated with the revelation of the Quran

ai.seo_question: On which days of Ramadan were the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran revealed?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes a hierarchical chronology of divine revelation, linking the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran to specific days in Ramadan, with the Quran’s revelation on Laylat al-Qadr marking its supreme status. This narrative reinforces the Shia emphasis on Ramadan as the month of the Quran’s descent, connecting the prophetic lineage through the specific timing of each scripture’s arrival. It serves as a theological basis for honoring the distinct spiritual merits of the earlier scriptures while affirming the Quran as the final and most significant revelation.
